subject: INLA binary install error on HPC cluster

messages.author: d7ee34c7589817da
messages.subject: INLA binary install error on HPC cluster
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to install INLA on a Linux HPC cluster using inla.binary.install() command. However, I got the following error:

Error in download.file(map.filename(fnm), to.file, quiet = TRUE) :
  download from 'https://inla.r-inla-download.org/Linux-builds/./CentOS%20Linux-7%20(Core)/Version_21.02.23/64bit.tgz' failed
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In download.file(map.filename(fnm), to.file, quiet = TRUE) :
  downloaded length 4479790 != reported length 59788637
2: In download.file(map.filename(fnm), to.file, quiet = TRUE) :
  URL 'https://inla.r-inla-download.org/Linux-builds/CentOS%20Linux-7%20(Core)/Version_21.02.23/64bit.tgz': status was 'Failed writing received data to disk/application'

The issue is I can do the binary install of INLA if my R library directory is in the home/ directory. However, I got the above error when I change my R library to my own project/ directory. It is not recommended to put packages in home/ server directory as this will potentially cause issue when running jobs as the HPC cluster does not handle jobs run from the home/ directory. Is there any way to get around this? Or is this a issue of the HPC server? Thanks!

David

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA binary install error on HPC cluster
parts:
You mentioned a potential issue with having R files under your user directory when running on the server. You can configure R to place and find your own-installed libraries in a different place. There are both environment variables (R_USER_LIB is think, but I may be wrong) and settings within R to control this.

Finn

messages.author: d7ee34c7589817da
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA binary install error on HPC cluster
parts:
Hi,

I have figured out the issue. The issue is not with inla.binary.install(). It is due to the fact that the directory where I put my packages has a very small disk quota (2MB). So the 64bit.tgz file of size 60MB cannot be properly downloaded. I should've checked this first. Sorry about that.

Thanks,
David

On Tuesday, July 6, 2021 at 4:18:31 AM UTC-4 he...@r-inla.org wrote:

R_LIBS_USER

On Tue, 2021-07-06 at 08:56 +0100, Finn Lindgren wrote:
> You mentioned a potential issue with having R files under your user
> directory when running on the server. You can configure R to place and
> find your own-installed libraries in a different place. There are both
> environment variables (R_USER_LIB is think, but I may be wrong) and
> settings within R to control this.

> Finn
